text:
Dear Partners,

There’s an old saying where I grew up: you don’t judge the harvest by the weather in July — you judge it by what’s still standing come frost. This quarter felt like an early frost. The central bank has held the policy rate at 5.25%, inflation is running at 3.8%, and high-yield spreads have widened out to 640bps. None of that is comfortable, but none of it is unfamiliar to those of us who've spent a career underwriting through cycles rather than around them.

On the portfolio: we reported a return of -2.0% for the quarter, bringing year-to-date to -3.5%. Since inception, we remain at +18.0%, and that number matters — it's the number that reflects what structural seniority is built to protect across a full horizon, not a single quarter. Public equities were down -3.0% over the same period, and while comparisons between our book and public markets are never quite apples to apples — our loans sit senior in the capital structure, secured, with covenants (loosening as they may be in places) that public equity holders simply don't have — we won't pretend the marks haven't been touched by the same weather everyone else is standing in.

We know many of you have seen secondary bids quoted well below our NAV index of 96.5. That gap is real, and we're not going to talk around it. Secondary markets in moments like this are thin, forced-seller markets — they price panic, not portfolios. Our NAV reflects par-plus-accrual on a loan book that remains, in the overwhelming majority, current and performing. We believe that gap will narrow as visibility improves, though we'd be lying if we told you it closes tomorrow.

You've also seen that we've gated redemptions this quarter. We don't do this lightly, and we don't do it to punish anyone standing with us. We do it because a fire sale of good collateral to satisfy a few exits is bad stewardship for everyone who stayed. This is what partnership means in practice — sometimes it means asking for patience precisely when patience is hardest to give.

On the amendment front, work continues in the spirit we described last quarter — constructive, collaborative, sponsor-aligned. We are not walking away from borrowers who are walking through a hard patch with us in good faith.

Looking ahead, we remain constructive on the medium-term outlook for the book, though we'd be imprudent not to flag that spreads this wide, held this long, could pressure weaker credits further before they heal. Should conditions deteriorate from here, we may see additional amendment activity, and we're watching the calendar closely. We don't traffic in promises. We traffic in seniority, structure, and time.

With respect and resolve,

Stonebeck Credit
